correctness.rationale: Exhaustive recursion over all 24 vertex choices visits 34,305 independent subsets uniquely. It proves alpha=10, 424 nine-sets, eight ten-sets, then generates every legal exchange and performs BFS from every state. A second checker enumerates all 24-choose-9 and 24-choose-10 subsets independently, constructs edges by pairwise symmetric-difference tests, checks no ten-set extends to eleven, and independently recomputes all distances. Complete independent outputs match: TJ9 1428 edges connected radius9 diameter11; TS9 1068 edges with components 416 and four K2; TJ10=TS10 two C4. Files were executed from actual packaged-source directory. The statements are exhaustive finite results, no inference beyond 24 vertices.

value.rationale: The unique cubic (3,7)-cage is a canonical extremal graph and maximum independent sets are a natural packing problem. This exact finite classification discovers a sharp transition: at size nine unrestricted jumps connect all 424 states while slides split into 5 components; at optimal packing size ten even jumps split all 8 states into two nontrivial four-cycles. This directly characterizes robustness of optimal packings and differs materially from the known state counts, homotopy, or generic model-equivalence lemma. No unproved large-graph consequence is suggested.
